details.all_issues:
Warning: The Dockerfile runs an editable install without dependency resolution and without pinning the project package:
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir --no-deps -e .
Why this is an issue: --no-deps causes pip to skip installing any dependency metadata declared by the project; if the earlier explicit pinned pip installs do not fully cover the project's required dependencies, the container build may produce a broken runtime. Also pip install -e . does not pin a specific version of the project package itself; the rubric requires installed packages and tools to be explicitly pinned for reproducibility. Recommended fixes: either install the project from a pinned package or install dependencies from a pinned requirements file or lockfile (e.g., use a committed requirements.txt with == pins or use the project's lockfile); remove --no-deps unless you intentionally manage all dependencies elsewhere.

Warning: The Dockerfile fetches external git repositories at build time (network fetch) even though the fetches are pinned to commits:
RUN set -e; \
    fetch() { \
      if [ ! -f "$1/$4" ]; then \
        rm -rf "$1" && git init -q "$1" \
          && git -C "$1" fetch -q --depth 1 "$2" "$3" \
          && git -C "$1" checkout -q FETCH_HEAD \
          && rm -rf "$1/.git"; \
      fi; \
    }; \
    fetch jedi/third_party/typeshed https://github.com/davidhalter/typeshed.git \
      4bb9d8351d0795fbc7dee3da069013a48641689d LICENSE; \
    fetch jedi/third_party/django-stubs https://github.com/davidhalter/django-stubs.git \
      fd057010f6cbf176f57d1099e82be46d39b99cb9 LICENSE.txt
Why this is an issue: While the fetches are pinned to specific commit SHAs (which is good for reproducibility), build-time network fetches require network access and the presence of git in the build image. If the build environment is air-gapped or the base image does not include git, this RUN will fail. It also increases build time and external dependency surface. Recommended fixes: vendor these submodules into the repository (so COPY . . includes them), ensure git is present in the build image, or document that network access is required for docker build. If keeping the fetch approach, the pinned SHAs mitigate non-determinism (good).

  - Rationale: The rubric warns for explicit build/install commands for interpreted languages (npm run build, pip install -e ., etc.). For Python projects an editable install during docker build is often unnecessary and can increase build time and makes the build do a project installation step that may not be needed for a development container. Consider installing dependencies only (via a pinned requirements.txt / lockfile) and leaving editable installs to the dev runtime, or justify why editable install is required during build.

WARNING: Potential unpinned dependencies risk from editable install line (may break reproducibility): RUN pip install --no-cache-dir --no-deps -e .

Details: The rubric warns when Dockerfiles run explicit build/install commands for interpreted languages (JavaScript/TypeScript/Python). Performing pip install -e . during docker build will run package setup/build steps at image build time. For typical interpreted-language development images it's often preferable to install only dependencies or rely on a developer performing editable installs at runtime, but editable installs can be acceptable if intentional. Recommendation: If you want a purely dependency-prepared image, consider installing pinned dependencies only (requirements.txt or pinned pip installs) and leave pip install -e . for interactive/dev use, or clearly document why an editable install at build time is required for your workflow.

+"""
+Choosing the overload of a function from the arguments of a call.
+"""
+
+from textwrap import dedent
+
+import pytest
+
+HEADER = """\
+from typing import overload, Any, Type, TypeVar, Union
+
+class A: pass
+class B(A): pass
+class C: pass
+class RA: pass
+class RB: pass
+class RC: pass
+"""
+
+
+def overloads(*annotations):
+    code = ''
+    for annotation, result in zip(annotations, ('RA', 'RB', 'RC')):
+        code += '@overload\ndef f(x: %s) -> %s: ...\n' % (annotation, result)
+    return code + 'def f(x): ...\n'
+
+
+def infer_result(Script, code):
+    code = HEADER + dedent(code).strip('\n')
+    lines = code.splitlines()
+    return sorted(d.name for d in Script(code).infer(len(lines), len(lines[-1])))
+
+
+def check(Script, annotations, call, expected, prefix=''):
+    code = prefix + overloads(*annotations) + call
+    assert infer_result(Script, code) == expected, (annotations, call)
+
+
+def test_issue_example(Script):
+    code = dedent('''\
+        from typing import overload
+
+        class Foo: pass
+
+        class FooBuilder:
+            def func_foo(self): pass
+
+        class Bar: pass
+
+        class BarBuilder:
+            def func_bar(self): pass
+
+        @overload
+        def get_obj(input: type[Foo]) -> FooBuilder: ...
+        @overload
+        def get_obj(input: type[Bar]) -> BarBuilder: ...
+        def get_obj(input: type): pass
+
+        builder = get_obj(Foo)
+        builder.''')
+    names = [c.name for c in Script(code).complete()]
+    assert 'func_foo' in names
+    assert 'func_bar' not in names
+
+    code = code.replace('get_obj(Foo)', 'get_obj(Bar)')
+    names = [c.name for c in Script(code).complete()]
+    assert 'func_bar' in names
+    assert 'func_foo' not in names
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('first', ['type[A]', 'Type[A]'])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    'call, expected', [
+        ('f(A)', ['RA']),
+        ('f(B)', ['RA']),
+        ('f(C)', ['RB']),
+    ]
+)
+def test_type_of_class(Script, first, call, expected):
+    check(Script, [first, 'type[C]'], call, expected)
+
+
+def test_type_rejects_instances(Script):
+    check(Script, ['type[A]', 'A'], 'f(A())', ['RB'])
+    check(Script, ['Type[A]', 'A'], 'f(B())', ['RB'])
+    check(Script, ['A', 'type[A]'], 'f(A)', ['RB'])
+    factory = 'class Factory:\n    def __call__(self) -> A: ...\n'
+    check(Script, ['type[A]', 'Factory'], 'f(Factory())', ['RB'], prefix=factory)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('annotation', ['type', 'Type', 'type[Any]', 'Type[Any]'])
+def test_any_class(Script, annotation):
+    for cls in ['A', 'B', 'C', 'int', 'str']:
+        check(Script, ['int', annotation], 'f(%s)' % cls, ['RB'])
+    for instance, cls in [('3', 'int'), ('C()', 'C'), ('"s"', 'str')]:
+        check(Script, [annotation, cls], 'f(%s)' % instance, ['RB'])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('annotation', ['type[Union[A, C]]', 'Type[A | C]', 'type[A] | type[C]'])
+def test_type_of_union(Script, annotation):
+    check(Script, ['int', annotation], 'f(C)', ['RB'])
+    check(Script, ['int', annotation], 'f(B)', ['RB'])
+
+
+def test_type_of_type_var(Script):
+    bound = 'T = TypeVar("T", bound=A)\n'
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'int'], 'f(C)', ['RA', 'RB'], prefix=bound)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[C]'], 'f(C)', ['RB'], prefix=bound)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[C]'], 'f(B)', ['RA'], prefix=bound)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[C]'], 'f(A)', ['RA'], prefix=bound)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'A'], 'f(B())', ['RB'], prefix=bound)
+    constrained = 'T = TypeVar("T", A, int)\n'
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[C]'], 'f(C)', ['RB'], prefix=constrained)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[C]'], 'f(int)', ['RA'], prefix=constrained)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[C]'], 'f(B)', ['RA'], prefix=constrained)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[str]'], 'f(str)', ['RB'], prefix=constrained)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'int'], 'f(3)', ['RB'], prefix=constrained)
+    unbound = 'T = TypeVar("T")\n'
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[C]'], 'f(C)', ['RA'], prefix=unbound)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[C]'], 'f(int)', ['RA'], prefix=unbound)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'int'], 'f(3)', ['RB'], prefix=unbound)
+
+
+def test_type_from_annotated_names(Script):
+    check(Script, ['type[A]', 'type[C]'], 'f(t)', ['RB'], prefix='t: type[C]\n')
+    code = overloads('type[A]', 'type[C]') + dedent('''\
+        def g(k: type[C]):
+            f(k)''')
+    assert infer_result(Script, code) == ['RB']
+
+
+def test_first_matching_overload_wins(Script):
+    check(Script, ['type[A]', 'type[B]'], 'f(B)', ['RA'])
+    check(Script, ['type[B]', 'type[A]'], 'f(B)', ['RA'])
+    check(Script, ['type[B]', 'type[A]'], 'f(A)', ['RB'])
+    check(Script, ['type', 'type[A]'], 'f(A)', ['RA'])
+    check(Script, ['type[A]', 'type[B]', 'type[C]'], 'f(C)', ['RC'])
+
+
+def test_type_keyword_argument(Script):
+    check(Script, ['int', 'type[C]'], 'f(x=C)', ['RB'])
+    check(Script, ['type[A]', 'type[B]'], 'f(x=B)', ['RA'])
+    check(Script, ['type[C]', 'int'], 'f(x=3)', ['RB'])
+
+
+TWO_PARAMETERS = '''\
+@overload
+def g(x: type[A], y: type[C]) -> RA: ...
+@overload
+def g(x: type[A], y: type[A]) -> RB: ...
+def g(x, y): ...
+'''
+
+
+def test_every_argument_has_to_fit(Script):
+    for call, expected in [
+        ('g(A, C)', ['RA']),
+        ('g(B, C)', ['RA']),
+        ('g(A, A)', ['RB']),
+        ('g(A, y=B)', ['RB']),
+        ('g(y=C, x=B)', ['RA']),
+        ('g(x=A, y=A)', ['RB']),
+        ('g(C, A)', ['RA', 'RB']),
+        ('g(A, A())', ['RA', 'RB']),
+    ]:
+        assert infer_result(Script, TWO_PARAMETERS + call) == expected, call
+
+
+def variadic(first, second, signature, third=None):
+    code = ''
+    for annotation, result in [(first, 'RA'), (second, 'RB'), (third, 'RC')]:
+        if annotation is not None:
+            code += '@overload\ndef f(%s) -> %s: ...\n' % (signature % annotation, result)
+    return code + 'def f(*args, **kwargs): ...\n'
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('signature', ['*x: %s', 'y: int, *x: %s'])
+def test_var_positional(Script, signature):
+    prefix = '1, ' if signature.startswith('y') else ''
+    for arguments, expected in [
+        ('C, C', ['RB']),
+        ('A, B', ['RA']),
+        ('A, C', ['RA', 'RB']),
+        ('C, A', ['RA', 'RB']),
+        ('', ['RA']),
+    ]:
+        call = 'f(%s)' % (prefix + arguments).rstrip(', ')
+        code = variadic('type[A]', 'type[C]', signature) + call
+        assert infer_result(Script, code) == expected, (signature, call)
+
+
+def test_var_positional_unpacked(Script):
+    code = variadic('type[A]', 'type[C]', '*x: %s')
+    assert infer_result(Script, code + 'ks = (C, C)\nf(*ks)') == ['RB']
+    assert infer_result(Script, code + 'ks = [A, B]\nf(*ks)') == ['RA']
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('signature', ['**x: %s', 'y: int, **x: %s'])
+def test_var_keyword(Script, signature):
+    prefix = 'y=1, ' if signature.startswith('y') else ''
+    for arguments, expected in [
+        ('p=C, q=C', ['RB']),
+        ('p=A, q=B', ['RA']),
+        ('p=A, q=C', ['RA', 'RB']),
+        ('', ['RA']),
+    ]:
+        call = 'f(%s)' % (prefix + arguments).rstrip(', ')
+        code = variadic('type[A]', 'type[C]', signature) + call
+        assert infer_result(Script, code) == expected, (signature, call)
+
+
+def test_var_keyword_unpacked(Script):
+    code = variadic('type[A]', 'type[C]', '**x: %s')
+    assert infer_result(Script, code + "f(**{'p': C})") == ['RB']
+
+
+def test_variadic_parameters_with_other_annotations(Script):
+    prefix = 'T = TypeVar("T", bound=A)\n'
+    code = prefix + variadic('type[T]', 'type[Union[A, C]]', '*x: %s')
+    assert infer_result(Script, code + 'f(A, B)') == ['RA']
+    assert infer_result(Script, code + 'f(A, C)') == ['RB']
+    assert infer_result(Script, code + 'f(C, int)') == ['RA', 'RB']
+    code = variadic('type', 'int', '*x: %s')
+    assert infer_result(Script, code + 'f(A, int, str)') == ['RA']
+    assert infer_result(Script, code + 'f(A, 1)') == ['RA', 'RB']
+    assert infer_result(Script, code + 'f(1, 2)') == ['RB']
+
+
+def test_variadic_parameters_together(Script):
+    code = dedent('''\
+        @overload
+        def f(y: int, *x: type[A], z: int = 0, **k: type[A]) -> RA: ...
+        @overload
+        def f(y: int, *x: type[C], z: int = 0, **k: type[C]) -> RB: ...
+        def f(*args, **kwargs): ...
+        ''')

+        ('f(1, C, z=2, p=C)', ['RB']),
+        ('f(1, A, p=C)', ['RA', 'RB']),
+        ('f(1, p=C)', ['RB']),
+        ('f(1, C)', ['RB']),
+        ('f(1, z=2)', ['RA']),
+    ]:

+def test_no_matching_overload(Script):

+    code = variadic('type[A]', 'type[C]', '*x: %s')

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Usage:
+#   ./test.sh [--output_path <junit.xml>] <base|new>
+#
+#   base  run the existing test suite.
+#   new   run the tests for choosing overloads from the call arguments.
+set -uo pipefail
+
+OUTPUT_PATH=""
+if [ "${1:-}" = "--output_path" ]; then
+  if [ -z "${2:-}" ]; then
+    echo "--output_path requires a value" >&2
+    exit 2
+  fi
+  case "$2" in
+    /*) OUTPUT_PATH="$2" ;;
+    *) OUTPUT_PATH="$PWD/$2" ;;
+  esac
+  shift 2
+fi
+
+MODE="${1:-new}"
+
+cd /app || exit 1
+
+NEW_TESTS="test/test_inference/test_gradual/test_overload_arguments_9c3e7a.py"
+
+PYTEST_ARGS=(-p no:cacheprovider -v)
+if [ -n "$OUTPUT_PATH" ]; then
+  if ! mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUTPUT_PATH")"; then
+    echo "failed to create the directory for $OUTPUT_PATH" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  PYTEST_ARGS+=(--junitxml="$OUTPUT_PATH")
+fi
+
+case "$MODE" in
+  base)
+    # The file path completion tests list the repository root, which also
+    # holds this script, and expanding "~" depends on the user's home folder.
+    python -m pytest "${PYTEST_ARGS[@]}" --ignore="$NEW_TESTS" \
+      --deselect test/test_api/test_completion.py::test_file_path_completions \
+      --deselect test/test_api/test_completion.py::test_complete_expanduser \
+      jedi test
+    STATUS=$?
+    ;;
+  new)
+    python -m pytest "${PYTEST_ARGS[@]}" "$NEW_TESTS"
+    STATUS=$?
+    ;;
+  *)

+    exit 2
+    ;;
+esac
+
+if [ -n "$OUTPUT_PATH" ] && [ ! -s "$OUTPUT_PATH" ]; then
+  echo "failed to write JUnit report to $OUTPUT_PATH" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+exit "$STATUS"

+"""
+Choosing the overload of a function from the arguments of a call.
+"""
+
+from textwrap import dedent
+
+import pytest
+
+HEADER = """\
+from typing import overload, Any, Type, TypeVar, Union
+
+class A: pass
+class B(A): pass
+class C: pass
+class RA: pass
+class RB: pass
+class RC: pass
+"""
+
+
+def overloads(*annotations):
+    code = ''
+    for annotation, result in zip(annotations, ('RA', 'RB', 'RC')):
+        code += '@overload\ndef f(x: %s) -> %s: ...\n' % (annotation, result)
+    return code + 'def f(x): ...\n'
+
+
+def infer_result(Script, code):
+    code = HEADER + dedent(code).strip('\n')
+    lines = code.splitlines()
+    return sorted(d.name for d in Script(code).infer(len(lines), len(lines[-1])))
+
+
+def check(Script, annotations, call, expected, prefix=''):
+    code = prefix + overloads(*annotations) + call
+    assert infer_result(Script, code) == expected, (annotations, call)
+
+
+def test_issue_example(Script):
+    code = dedent('''\
+        from typing import overload
+
+        class Foo: pass
+
+        class FooBuilder:
+            def func_foo(self): pass
+
+        class Bar: pass
+
+        class BarBuilder:
+            def func_bar(self): pass
+
+        @overload
+        def get_obj(input: type[Foo]) -> FooBuilder: ...
+        @overload
+        def get_obj(input: type[Bar]) -> BarBuilder: ...
+        def get_obj(input: type): pass
+
+        builder = get_obj(Foo)
+        builder.''')
+    names = [c.name for c in Script(code).complete()]
+    assert 'func_foo' in names
+    assert 'func_bar' not in names
+
+    code = code.replace('get_obj(Foo)', 'get_obj(Bar)')
+    names = [c.name for c in Script(code).complete()]
+    assert 'func_bar' in names
+    assert 'func_foo' not in names
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('first', ['type[A]', 'Type[A]'])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    'call, expected', [
+        ('f(A)', ['RA']),
+        ('f(B)', ['RA']),
+        ('f(C)', ['RB']),
+    ]
+)
+def test_type_of_class(Script, first, call, expected):
+    check(Script, [first, 'type[C]'], call, expected)
+
+
+def test_type_rejects_instances(Script):
+    check(Script, ['type[A]', 'A'], 'f(A())', ['RB'])
+    check(Script, ['Type[A]', 'A'], 'f(B())', ['RB'])
+    check(Script, ['A', 'type[A]'], 'f(A)', ['RB'])
+    factory = 'class Factory:\n    def __call__(self) -> A: ...\n'
+    check(Script, ['type[A]', 'Factory'], 'f(Factory())', ['RB'], prefix=factory)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('annotation', ['type', 'Type', 'type[Any]', 'Type[Any]'])
+def test_any_class(Script, annotation):
+    for cls in ['A', 'B', 'C', 'int', 'str']:
+        check(Script, ['int', annotation], 'f(%s)' % cls, ['RB'])
+    for instance, cls in [('3', 'int'), ('C()', 'C'), ('"s"', 'str')]:
+        check(Script, [annotation, cls], 'f(%s)' % instance, ['RB'])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('annotation', ['type[Union[A, C]]', 'Type[A | C]', 'type[A] | type[C]'])
+def test_type_of_union(Script, annotation):
+    check(Script, ['int', annotation], 'f(C)', ['RB'])
+    check(Script, ['int', annotation], 'f(B)', ['RB'])
+
+
+def test_type_of_type_var(Script):
+    bound = 'T = TypeVar("T", bound=A)\n'
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'int'], 'f(C)', ['RA', 'RB'], prefix=bound)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[C]'], 'f(C)', ['RB'], prefix=bound)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[C]'], 'f(B)', ['RA'], prefix=bound)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[C]'], 'f(A)', ['RA'], prefix=bound)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'A'], 'f(B())', ['RB'], prefix=bound)

+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[C]'], 'f(C)', ['RB'], prefix=constrained)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[C]'], 'f(int)', ['RA'], prefix=constrained)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[C]'], 'f(B)', ['RA'], prefix=constrained)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[str]'], 'f(str)', ['RB'], prefix=constrained)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'int'], 'f(3)', ['RB'], prefix=constrained)

+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[C]'], 'f(C)', ['RA'], prefix=unbound)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[C]'], 'f(int)', ['RA'], prefix=unbound)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'int'], 'f(3)', ['RB'], prefix=unbound)
+
+
+def test_type_from_annotated_names(Script):
+    check(Script, ['type[A]', 'type[C]'], 'f(t)', ['RB'], prefix='t: type[C]\n')
+    code = overloads('type[A]', 'type[C]') + dedent('''\
+        def g(k: type[C]):
+            f(k)''')

+
+
+def test_first_matching_overload_wins(Script):

+    check(Script, ['type[B]', 'type[A]'], 'f(B)', ['RA'])

+
+
+def test_type_keyword_argument(Script):
+    check(Script, ['int', 'type[C]'], 'f(x=C)', ['RB'])
+    check(Script, ['type[A]', 'type[B]'], 'f(x=B)', ['RA'])
+    check(Script, ['type[C]', 'int'], 'f(x=3)', ['RB'])
+
+
+TWO_PARAMETERS = '''\
+@overload
+def g(x: type[A], y: type[C]) -> RA: ...
+@overload
+def g(x: type[A], y: type[A]) -> RB: ...
+def g(x, y): ...
+'''
+
+
+def test_every_argument_has_to_fit(Script):
+    for call, expected in [
+        ('g(A, C)', ['RA']),
+        ('g(B, C)', ['RA']),
+        ('g(A, A)', ['RB']),
+        ('g(A, y=B)', ['RB']),
+        ('g(y=C, x=B)', ['RA']),
+        ('g(x=A, y=A)', ['RB']),
+        ('g(C, A)', ['RA', 'RB']),
+        ('g(A, A())', ['RA', 'RB']),
+    ]:
+        assert infer_result(Script, TWO_PARAMETERS + call) == expected, call
+
+
+def variadic(first, second, signature, third=None):
+    code = ''
+    for annotation, result in [(first, 'RA'), (second, 'RB'), (third, 'RC')]:
+        if annotation is not None:
+            code += '@overload\ndef f(%s) -> %s: ...\n' % (signature % annotation, result)
+    return code + 'def f(*args, **kwargs): ...\n'
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('signature', ['*x: %s', 'y: int, *x: %s'])
+def test_var_positional(Script, signature):
+    prefix = '1, ' if signature.startswith('y') else ''
+    for arguments, expected in [
+        ('C, C', ['RB']),
+        ('A, B', ['RA']),
+        ('A, C', ['RA', 'RB']),
+        ('C, A', ['RA', 'RB']),
+        ('', ['RA']),
+    ]:
+        call = 'f(%s)' % (prefix + arguments).rstrip(', ')

+
+
+def test_var_positional_unpacked(Script):
+    code = variadic('type[A]', 'type[C]', '*x: %s')
+    assert infer_result(Script, code + 'ks = (C, C)\nf(*ks)') == ['RB']
+    assert infer_result(Script, code + 'ks = [A, B]\nf(*ks)') == ['RA']
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('signature', ['**x: %s', 'y: int, **x: %s'])
+def test_var_keyword(Script, signature):
+    prefix = 'y=1, ' if signature.startswith('y') else ''
+    for arguments, expected in [
+        ('p=C, q=C', ['RB']),
+        ('p=A, q=B', ['RA']),
+        ('p=A, q=C', ['RA', 'RB']),
+        ('', ['RA']),
+    ]:
+        call = 'f(%s)' % (prefix + arguments).rstrip(', ')
+        code = variadic('type[A]', 'type[C]', signature) + call
+        assert infer_result(Script, code) == expected, (signature, call)
+
+
+def test_var_keyword_unpacked(Script):
+    code = variadic('type[A]', 'type[C]', '**x: %s')
+    assert infer_result(Script, code + "f(**{'p': C})") == ['RB']
+
+
+def test_variadic_parameters_with_other_annotations(Script):
+    prefix = 'T = TypeVar("T", bound=A)\n'
+    code = prefix + variadic('type[T]', 'type[Union[A, C]]', '*x: %s')
+    assert infer_result(Script, code + 'f(A, B)') == ['RA']
+    assert infer_result(Script, code + 'f(A, C)') == ['RB']
+    assert infer_result(Script, code + 'f(C, int)') == ['RA', 'RB']
+    code = variadic('type', 'int', '*x: %s')
+    assert infer_result(Script, code + 'f(A, int, str)') == ['RA']
+    assert infer_result(Script, code + 'f(A, 1)') == ['RA', 'RB']
+    assert infer_result(Script, code + 'f(1, 2)') == ['RB']
+
+
+def test_variadic_parameters_together(Script):
+    code = dedent('''\
+        @overload
+        def f(y: int, *x: type[A], z: int = 0, **k: type[A]) -> RA: ...
+        @overload
+        def f(y: int, *x: type[C], z: int = 0, **k: type[C]) -> RB: ...
+        def f(*args, **kwargs): ...
+        ''')
+    for call, expected in [
+        ('f(1, A, B, p=A)', ['RA']),
+        ('f(1, C, z=2, p=C)', ['RB']),
+        ('f(1, A, p=C)', ['RA', 'RB']),
+        ('f(1, p=C)', ['RB']),
+        ('f(1, C)', ['RB']),
+        ('f(1, z=2)', ['RA']),

+
+def test_no_matching_overload(Script):
+    check(Script, ['type[A]', 'int'], 'f(C)', ['RA', 'RB'])

+
+def test_dict_unpacking(Script):

+

+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('annotation', ['type', 'Type', 'type[Any]', 'Type[Any]'])

+        class K:

+    assert infer_result(Script, code + 'functools.partial(f, q=A)(**dict(p=C))') == ['RA', 'RB']
+
+
+CONTAINERS = 'import random\nfrom typing import Iterable, List, Mapping, Sequence\n'
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('first, second, call', [
+    ('list[type[A]]', 'list[type[C]]', 'f([C])'),
+    ('List[Type[A]]', 'List[Type[C]]', 'x = [C, C]\nf(x)'),
+    ('Sequence[type[A]]', 'Sequence[type[C]]', 'f((C, C))'),
+    ('Iterable[type[A]]', 'Iterable[type[C]]', 'f({C})'),
+    ('tuple[type[A], ...]', 'tuple[type[C], ...]', 'f((C, C))'),

+    ('Mapping[str, type[A]]', 'Mapping[str, type[C]]', 'f(dict(k=C))'),
+    ('dict[str, list[type[A]]]', 'dict[str, list[type[C]]]', 'f({"k": [C]})'),
+])
+def test_elements_of_containers(Script, first, second, call):
+    check(Script, [first, second, 'object'], call, ['RB'], prefix=CONTAINERS)
+    if not call.startswith('x ='):
+        # Classes are accepted with their subclasses.
+        check(Script, [first, second, 'object'], call.replace('C', 'B'), ['RA'],
+              prefix=CONTAINERS)
+
+
+def test_every_element_has_to_fit(Script):
+    annotations = ['list[type[A]]', 'list[type[C]]', 'object']
+    for call in [
+        'f([A, C])',
+        'f([C()])',
+        'f((C,))',
+        'f([C] if random.random() else [A])',
+        'f([C if random.random() else A])',
+    ]:
+        check(Script, annotations, call, ['RC'], prefix=CONTAINERS)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('first, second, call, expected', [
+    ('tuple[type[A], ...]', 'tuple[type[C], ...]', 'f((C,))', ['RB']),
+    ('tuple[type[A], ...]', 'tuple[type[C], ...]', 'f((C, C, C))', ['RB']),
+    ('Tuple[Type[A], ...]', 'Tuple[Type[C], ...]', 'f((C,))', ['RB']),
+    ('tuple[int, ...]', 'tuple[str, ...]', 'f(("a", "b"))', ['RB']),
+    ('tuple[int, ...]', 'tuple[str, ...]', 'f((1, 2, 3))', ['RA']),
+    ('tuple[type[A], ...]', 'tuple[type[C], ...]', 'f((B, A))', ['RA']),
+    ('tuple[type[A], ...]', 'tuple[type[C], ...]', 'f((A, C))', ['RC']),
+    ('tuple[type[A], type[A]]', 'tuple[type[C], ...]', 'f((C, C))', ['RB']),
+    ('tuple[type[C], ...]', 'object', 'f(())', ['RA']),
+])
+def test_tuples_of_any_length(Script, first, second, call, expected):
+    prefix = CONTAINERS + 'from typing import Tuple\n'
+    check(Script, [first, second, 'object'], call, expected, prefix=prefix)
+
+
+def test_items_of_mappings_and_other_containers(Script):
+    def check_items(first, second, call, expected=['RB'], prefix=''):
+        check(Script, [first, second, 'object'], call, expected, prefix=CONTAINERS + prefix)
+
+    check_items('dict[type[A], int]', 'dict[type[C], int]', 'f({C: 1})')
+    check_items('dict[str, type[A]]', 'dict[int, type[A]]', 'f({1: A})')
+    check_items('dict[str, type[A]]', 'dict[str, type[C]]', 'f({"k": C, **{"m": C}})')
+    check_items('Sequence[type[A]]', 'Sequence[type[C]]', 'f(g())',
+                prefix='def g() -> tuple[type[C], ...]: ...\n')
+    check_items('list[type[T]]', 'list[type[C]]', 'f([C])',
+                prefix='T = TypeVar("T", bound=A)\n')
+
+
+def test_protocol_annotations_are_structural(Script):
+    prefix = dedent('''\
+        from typing import Protocol
+        class Runner(Protocol):
+            def run(self) -> int: ...
+        class Good:
+            def run(self) -> int: return 1
+        class Bad: pass
+        ''')
+    check(Script, ['Runner', 'object'], 'f(Good())', ['RA'], prefix=prefix)
+    check(Script, ['Runner', 'object'], 'f(Bad())', ['RB'], prefix=prefix)
+
+
+def test_dict_call_accepts_all_pair_iterables(Script):
+    code = variadic('type[A]', 'type[C]', '**x: %s')
+    assert infer_result(Script, code + 'f(**dict([["p", C], ["q", C]]))') == ['RB']
+    assert infer_result(
+        Script, code + 'f(**dict((k, C) for k in ("p", "q")))'
+    ) == ['RB']
+
+
+def test_fixed_tuple_slots_and_length(Script):
+    check(
+        Script,
+        ['tuple[type[A], type[C]]', 'tuple[type[C], type[A]]'],
+        'f((C, A))',
+        ['RB'],
+    )
+    check(
+        Script,
+        ['tuple[type[A], type[C]]', 'object'],
+        'f((A, C, C))',
+        ['RB'],
+    )
+
+
+def test_var_keyword_parameter_name_is_collected(Script):
+    code = variadic('type[A]', 'type[C]', '**x: %s')
+    assert infer_result(Script, code + 'f(x=C)') == ['RB']
+
+
+def test_partial_call_keyword_overrides_bound_keyword(Script):
+    code = dedent('''\
+        import functools
+        @overload
+        def f(*, x: type[A]) -> RA: ...
+        @overload
+        def f(*, x: type[C]) -> RB: ...
+        def f(**kwargs): ...
+        ''')
+    assert infer_result(Script, code + 'functools.partial(f, x=A)(x=C)') == ['RB']
+    assert infer_result(Script, code + 'functools.partial(f, x=A)(**dict(x=C))') == ['RB']

output.authorGuidance:
Expand starred members when a list or tuple is itself unpacked into a call. Today `f(*[*[A], C])` drops `A` before overload matching and can select the `type[C]` overload. Also avoid turning still-known nested `dict(...)` contents into an unknown empty value solely because a fixed recursion depth was reached.

Strengthen the tests with mixed-type unpacking cases. Add a starred sequence such as `[C, *[A]]` and a mapping such as `{"k": C, **{"m": A}}`; both should reject the specialized container overloads and use the fallback. The current same-type mapping case cannot detect an implementation that ignores all `**` entries.

The agent runs otherwise show a deliberately hard, fair task. Most near-misses were around generic-container compatibility and keyword replacement in `dict(...)` or `functools.partial`, not hidden requirements. Keep the clear behavioral specification, broad annotation coverage, strict first-match design, robust harness, and baseline-regression coverage.

The requested outcome is explicit: select the first overload whose argument annotations accept all invocation arguments, otherwise combine overload results. The description also defines the expected handling of `type[...]`, TypeVars, Optional, generic containers, unions, variadic parameters, unpacking, `dict(...)`, and `functools.partial`, which gives a developer a substantive behavioral specification.

The test patch’s behavioral cases track the stated requirements: class-versus-instance matching and subclass acceptance, all-possible-type checks, generic containers, argument binding by position/name, variadics, tuple/list/dict unpacking, supported `dict(...)` forms, and partial calls are all described in the prompt. A correct implementation requires tracing how parsed call arguments are unpacked and bound to parameters, how annotations are represented and compared, how overload results are selected, and how wrappers such as partials preserve or replace arguments. The relevant code is distributed across `arguments.py`, `param.py`, `signature.py`, gradual typing modules, and stdlib plugins, so this is not solvable as an isolated edit.

requirements.sourceQuote: With `type[T]` where `T` is TypeVar, the class must satisfy the bounds or one of the constraints of `T`; If `T` has no bounds and no constraints, then all classes are accepted.
requirements.text: For type[T], bounded and constrained TypeVars restrict accepted classes accordingly, while an unconstrained TypeVar accepts every class.

output.summary: Audited the specification, the 61-test verifier, the reference implementation, the full 3,981-test base suite, and adversarial probes. The original verifier strongly covers type[X]/Type[X], subclass-vs-instance behavior, Any-class forms, TypeVar bounds/constraints, Optional, first-match/fall-through ordering, positional/keyword/multi-valued arguments, direct and unpacked variadics, many dict(...) forms, methods/classmethods/partial, and homogeneous/nested containers. Five real blind spots remain. A single plausible broken implementation combining those five shortcuts passed all original verifier tests (61/61) and the full base suite (3,955 passed, 21 skipped, 5 xfailed), while reference probes diverged on every blind spot. The replacement /var/artifacts/updated_test.patch adds five tests; it applies cleanly to the pristine checkout, all 66 tests pass with the reference, and all five added tests fail against the demonstrated broken implementation.

output.taskSummary: The task is to make Jedi choose an overloaded function’s return type from the call’s inferred argument types. A candidate overload matches only when all supplied arguments fit their annotations; the first matching overload wins, and if none matches, results from all overloads are combined. The prompt also specifies type[X]/TypeVar behavior, Optional, generic containers, union-valued arguments, variadic and unpacked arguments, dict(...) construction, and functools.partial. The new tests exercise those behaviors through inferred return-type names and code completion.

tests.evidence: The prompt’s motivating example says get_obj(Foo) should suggest only FooBuilder methods, not BarBuilder methods, and the analogous overload should be selected for Bar.
tests.name: test_issue_example
tests.qualityCheck: Checks both directions using completion-visible methods, so an implementation returning both overload results fails.
tests.verifies: For get_obj(Foo), completion includes func_foo and excludes func_bar; after changing the call to get_obj(Bar), it includes func_bar and excludes func_foo.

tests.evidence: The prompt states that type[X] accepts class X and its subclasses; the overload rule selects the first matching overload. Type[A] is also explicitly exercised by the prompt’s stated Type spelling.
tests.name: test_type_of_class
tests.qualityCheck: Covers the exact class, a subclass, and an unrelated class for both spellings.
tests.verifies: With the first parameter annotated type[A] or Type[A] and the second type[C], f(A) and f(B) infer only RA, while f(C) infers only RB.

tests.evidence: The prompt explicitly says a type[X] parameter accepts class X and subclasses, not instances. Its first-matching-overload rule determines which of these competing signatures supplies the result.
tests.name: test_type_rejects_instances
tests.qualityCheck: Useful positive and negative checks; the factory case additionally distinguishes a callable that produces A from a class argument.
tests.verifies: For four specified overload pairs and calls, an instance (including Factory()) is rejected by the type[A] / Type[A] overload and the expected ordinary-instance overload alone is inferred; class A passed to type[A] is not accepted by the ordinary A overload.

tests.evidence: The prompt states that type, Type, and type[Any] accept all classes, while type[X] accepts classes rather than instances. Its overload rule explains the expected competing-overload result.
tests.name: test_any_class
tests.qualityCheck: Samples several unrelated class objects and separately checks that broad class annotations do not thereby accept instances.
tests.verifies: For each of type, Type, type[Any], and Type[Any], class arguments A, B, C, int, and str select the second overload; instance arguments 3, C(), and "s" also select the second overload when the competing overload accepts that instance.

tests.evidence: Python typing semantics for Type[C] with a union C treat it as accepting class objects corresponding to the union alternatives; B is a subclass of A. The prompt supplies the type[X]/subclass and first-match rules, but does not spell out the inner-union spelling, so that part relies on standard typing semantics.
tests.name: test_type_of_union
tests.qualityCheck: Exercises three equivalent union spellings and a subclass case; the union interpretation is an external typing convention rather than a separately quoted prompt rule.
tests.verifies: For each of type[Union[A, C]], Type[A | C], and type[A] | type[C], f(C) and f(B) infer only RB rather than the preceding int overload.

tests.evidence: The prompt says type[T] requires the class to satisfy T’s bounds or one of its constraints, and that an unbounded, unconstrained T accepts all classes. It also states the first-match and no-match fallback rules.
tests.name: test_type_of_type_var
tests.qualityCheck: Covers bounded, constrained, and unconstrained TypeVars, including subclasses and instances; it is a useful breadth check rather than a single-case assertion.
tests.verifies: With a bound TypeVar, constrained TypeVar, or unbounded TypeVar, each listed class or instance call infers the exact specified RA, RB, or combined RA/RB result for the type[T] overload versus the competing overload.

tests.evidence: The prompt requires choosing based on whether each invocation argument matches its annotation. The scenario supplies the argument’s type through an explicit type[C] annotation, so type[C] matches and type[A] does not.
tests.name: test_type_from_annotated_names
tests.qualityCheck: Checks both module-level and function-parameter annotated names, though it uses only one annotated class type.
tests.verifies: A variable annotated type[C], including a function parameter k: type[C], passed to f(type[A] overload, type[C] overload) infers only RB.

tests.evidence: The prompt says the first overload where every invocation argument matches is used. It also states the accepted class/subclass behavior and that type accepts all classes.
tests.name: test_first_matching_overload_wins
tests.qualityCheck: Specifically discriminates declaration order and a broad earlier overload from implementations that combine all matching overloads.
tests.verifies: The six calls infer exactly RA, RA, RB, RA, and RC as listed, including cases where both type[B] and type[A] could accept B and where broad type precedes type[A].

tests.evidence: The prompt explicitly includes arguments supplied by name in the rule that every invocation argument must match an overload annotation, and specifies first-match selection.
tests.name: test_type_keyword_argument
tests.qualityCheck: A concise check of keyword binding with both class and instance values.
tests.verifies: For each x=... call, the named argument is matched against the overload parameter x and the exact expected single result is inferred: RB, RA, and RB respectively.

tests.evidence: The prompt requires every invocation argument, whether positional or named, to match. It says to choose the first matching overload, and to combine results only when no overload matches.
tests.name: test_every_argument_has_to_fit
tests.qualityCheck: Includes a case where one argument rules out an otherwise plausible signature and cases where no overload matches; sorting means the combined result is tested as a set of names, not an ordering.
tests.verifies: For the eight listed two-argument positional and keyword call forms, the exact inferred results are RA, RA, RB, RB, RA, RB, both RA and RB, and both RA and RB, respectively.

tests.evidence: The prompt says annotations for arguments received through *args are aggregated and that an overload still matches when *args receives no arguments.
tests.name: test_var_positional
tests.qualityCheck: Tests multiple collected values, their order-independent aggregate compatibility, an empty variadic argument, and both signature layouts.
tests.verifies: For both *x: annotation and a fixed y:int followed by *x: annotation, each listed call infers the exact expected result; every collected variadic positional value is checked, and the empty variadic call selects RA.

tests.evidence: The prompt explicitly counts arguments unpacked from a tuple or list at the call and says *args annotations are aggregated; it also specifies class/subclass acceptance.
tests.name: test_var_positional_unpacked
tests.qualityCheck: Covers both tuple and list sources; both assertions are direct return-type checks.
tests.verifies: Unpacking ks=(C,C) into f(*ks) infers RB; unpacking ks=[A,B] infers RA.

tests.evidence: The prompt says annotations for arguments received through **kwargs are aggregated and an overload still matches when **kwargs receives no arguments.
tests.name: test_var_keyword
tests.qualityCheck: Tests multiple keyword values, incompatible mixtures, an empty variadic mapping, and both signature layouts.
tests.verifies: For both **x: annotation and a fixed y:int followed by **x: annotation, each listed call infers the exact expected result; all supplied keyword values are considered, and the empty **x call selects RA.

tests.evidence: The prompt explicitly counts arguments unpacked from a dict at the call and requires **kwargs values to match the corresponding annotation.
tests.name: test_var_keyword_unpacked
tests.qualityCheck: A fair but shallow single-value unpacking case; other tests provide broader dict coverage.
tests.verifies: Calling f(**{'p': C}) against **x: type[A] and **x: type[C] infers only RB.

tests.evidence: The prompt says all variadic arguments are aggregated and each invocation argument must match; it also specifies TypeVar bounds and the class/subclass behavior of type[X].
tests.name: test_variadic_parameters_with_other_annotations
tests.qualityCheck: Combines variadic aggregation with nontrivial annotations and distinguishes a first match from fallback combination.
tests.verifies: For the listed type[T], type[Union[A,C]], type, and int variadic overload pairs, each multi-argument call infers exactly the asserted RA, RB, both, or single result.

tests.evidence: The prompt specifies aggregation for both *args and **kwargs, requires every invocation argument to match, and explicitly says empty *args or **kwargs does not prevent a match.
tests.name: test_variadic_parameters_together
tests.qualityCheck: Covers interaction between fixed, variadic positional, and variadic keyword parameters; the empty-variadic behavior is tested with fixed arguments present.
tests.verifies: For each listed call containing y, optional z, *x, and **k, the exact result is inferred: RA, RB, both RA/RB, RB, RB, or RA as specified; empty *x/**k calls still allow a match.

tests.evidence: The prompt states that the first matching overload is used and that results from all overloads are combined only if no overload matches.
tests.name: test_no_matching_overload
tests.qualityCheck: Directly distinguishes matching from fallback behavior, including a variadic no-match case.
tests.verifies: f(C) and f(A, C, int) infer both RA and RB when no overload matches, while f(A) infers only RA when the first overload matches.

tests.evidence: The prompt explicitly includes dicts created by dict(...) and says **kwargs values are aggregated and must match the annotation.
tests.name: test_dict_unpacking
tests.qualityCheck: Checks direct and assigned dict construction, including a mixed-value dict that matches neither overload.
tests.verifies: The four calls f(**dict(p=C)), f(**dict(p=A)), assignment then f(**d), and f(**dict(p=A,q=C)) infer RB, RA, RB, and both RA/RB respectively.

tests.evidence: The prompt says Optional[X] accepts None and any value accepted by X; first matching overload selection determines the result.
tests.name: test_optional_accepts_none
tests.qualityCheck: Checks both the None case and an X value, plus a competing non-Optional value.
tests.verifies: With Optional[int] and str overloads, f(None) and f(1) infer RA, while f("") infers RB.

tests.evidence: The prompt explicitly requires accounting for dict(...) in its supported call forms. The duplicate-key case also relies on Python dict-constructor semantics: a keyword value replaces the same key supplied by the positional mapping. The overload result then follows the prompt’s matching rule.
tests.name: test_dict_positional_argument
tests.qualityCheck: Broad set of dict construction forms. The assertion for the duplicate key is especially useful because it distinguishes final mapping contents from naïvely aggregating both values.
tests.verifies: The listed dict construction and unpacking calls infer RB, RA, both RA/RB, or RB exactly as asserted, including mapping/iterable positional forms, keyword additions, and a duplicate key overridden by a keyword value.

tests.evidence: The prompt applies argument matching and dict-created **kwargs to overloaded functions; nothing restricts those rules to module-level functions. The method calls supply the specified type[C] or type[A] value.
tests.name: test_dict_unpacking_in_method
tests.qualityCheck: Covers both method binding and two dict construction forms.
tests.verifies: K().f(**dict(p=C)) infers only RB, and K().f(**dict([('p', A)])) infers only RA.

tests.evidence: The prompt explicitly says that if a passed argument can have multiple types, such as a Union, the overload annotation must accept all of those types.
tests.name: test_union_argument
tests.qualityCheck: Tests rejection when only one union member fits, acceptance by an annotation covering the union, and a subtype/union interaction.
tests.verifies: When g(A()) has inferred return types Union[A,C], the three overload pairs infer both RA/RB, only RA, and only RB respectively.

tests.evidence: The prompt says type/Type/type[Any] accepts all classes and type[X] accepts subclasses of X but not instances.
tests.name: test_any_class_defined_later
tests.qualityCheck: Checks a later-defined subclass as both a class object and an instance.
tests.verifies: For each broad class annotation, f(D) selects RB and f(D()) selects RB when D is defined as a subclass of C.

tests.evidence: The prompt states that Optional[X] accepts None and any value X accepts; type[X] accepts subclasses, and the overload rule selects the first matching annotation.
tests.name: test_optional_of_class
tests.qualityCheck: Exercises None, an A subclass instance, and a competing unrelated instance.
tests.verifies: With Optional[A] and C overloads, f(B()) and f(None) infer RA; f(C()) infers RB.

tests.evidence: The prompt requires variadic annotations to aggregate every argument and requires all invocation argument types to be accepted; type[A] also accepts subclasses such as B.
tests.name: test_every_collected_argument_is_checked
tests.qualityCheck: Specifically ensures a later value is not ignored after earlier values have matched. The random expressions elsewhere are static source alternatives, not random runtime test inputs.
tests.verifies: For both *x and **x overload pairs, a final C value makes the type[A] overload fail and selects the broad type overload, while a final B value leaves only the type[A] overload result RA.

tests.evidence: The prompt’s overload argument and dict-unpacking rules apply to these calls; the classmethod calls provide the corresponding class objects as **kwargs values.
tests.name: test_dict_unpacking_in_classmethod
tests.qualityCheck: Adds classmethod and bound-instance call forms to the method coverage.
tests.verifies: K.f(**dict(p=C)) and K().f(**dict(p=A)) infer RB and RA respectively.

tests.evidence: The prompt says the overload argument rules also apply through functools.partial and that dict-created unpacked arguments count.
tests.name: test_dict_unpacking_in_partial
tests.qualityCheck: Covers a partial with no stored arguments, a stored compatible keyword, and a mixed case that matches neither overload.
tests.verifies: For the three partial calls shown, unpacked dict values infer RB, RA, and both RA/RB respectively, including a stored keyword combined with a later **dict call.

tests.evidence: Python functools.partial semantics specify that keywords supplied at call time override keywords stored in the partial; the prompt then applies overload selection to the resulting call arguments.
tests.name: test_keyword_replaced_in_partial
tests.qualityCheck: Tests replacement across direct, unpacked, and nested-partial forms, rather than merely testing one replacement spelling.
tests.verifies: Each of four calls, including a nested partial and both explicit and **-unpacked call keywords, infers exactly the result for the later x value: C selects RB and A selects RA.

tests.evidence: The prompt says every element of a container argument must be accepted by its corresponding annotation and specifically requires both dict keys and values to be accepted; type[X] accepts subclasses.
tests.name: test_elements_of_containers
tests.qualityCheck: Broad container-family coverage, including a nested value container and subclass substitutions. The preassigned x=[C,C] case intentionally omits the replacement subcase.
tests.verifies: For each of eight container annotations and calls, the C-valued argument selects RB; where the test also substitutes B, it selects RA. The cases include list, List, Sequence, Iterable, variadic tuple, dict key/value, Mapping, and nested dict/list annotations.

tests.evidence: The prompt requires every container element to satisfy the corresponding annotation and requires annotations to accept all possible types when an argument can have multiple types.
tests.name: test_every_element_has_to_fit
tests.qualityCheck: Checks mixed elements, an instance element, and conditional alternatives. The random calls are analyzed as source expressions; the test does not depend on runtime randomness.
tests.verifies: For each of five list arguments containing incompatible or alternative element types, neither list[type[A]] nor list[type[C]] matches, so only the fallback object overload result RC is inferred.

tests.evidence: The prompt says every element of a container argument must be accepted by its corresponding annotation; the empty tuple has no violating elements. The first-match/fallback rules determine the listed return types.
tests.name: test_tuples_of_any_length
tests.qualityCheck: Covers tuple length variation, fixed and variadic tuple annotations, and the empty tuple case.
tests.verifies: For each of nine tuple calls and annotation pairs, the exact result is the listed RA, RB, or RC; this includes one-, three-, and zero-element tuples, fixed-length and ellipsis tuple annotations, and incompatible elements.

tests.evidence: The prompt requires both dict keys and values, every container element, and type[T] classes to satisfy bounds. Its overload rule determines that the matching second overload’s RB result is inferred.
tests.name: test_items_of_mappings_and_other_containers
tests.qualityCheck: Adds key-position checking, annotated iterable contents, and a bounded TypeVar nested inside a container.
tests.verifies: The listed calls require matching dict key and value types, infer a tuple-of-type[C] return through a Sequence annotation, and accept list[type[T]] with T bounded by A; each call is asserted to infer RB.
